riddles.text: Every face in this city wears one, and nobody reads it aloud. Bring me one long enough to need four of your digits.
hints: Letters need it to find their way home.
It hangs beside a door, on a gate, or over a shop.
A street number with four or more digits, photographed where it hangs.

riddles.text: I speak three words and never finish a sentence. The drivers listen. The walkers wait for my smaller cousin.
hints: I stand at the corner and I never sleep.
Red, amber, green.
A traffic light: the drivers' signal, not the walking figure.

riddles.text: Tonight half the city is lying about who they are. Catch one of the liars in the act.
hints: The lie is sewn, painted, or glued on.
Look for someone who came as something else.
A person in costume. Ask before you take the photo.

riddles.text: A door no one knocks on, cut for a guest who never uses the handle. Prove your hand is bigger than its welcome.
hints: The guest has four legs.
It swings both ways, set into a bigger door.
A pet flap, with your hand beside it for scale.

riddles.text: Tomorrow I will be wrong, and someone will wipe me away. Find where tonight is written in something that does not last.
hints: Look for a hand, not a printer.
Chalkboards, whiteboards, marker on card.
Today's date, handwritten somewhere temporary.

riddles.text: Some of this city would fall if it were let go. Show me what is holding on.
hints: Look up.
Wires, bolts, brackets, scaffolds.
Anything braced, cabled, or bolted to stop it falling.

riddles.text: The planners drew a promise in straight lines. Find where they broke it.
hints: The map says go on. The ground says no.
A dead end, a road that stops, a stair to nowhere.
A place where a street or path simply ends.

riddles.text: An eye, open and awake, with no one behind it.
hints: The city has thousands of these after dark.
Glass, lit from inside.
A lit window with nobody in view: an empty room, a closed shop.

riddles.text: I was here before the road, and the road was laid around me.
hints: Age shows in the edges.
Carved or cut, set into a wall or the ground.
Worked stone older than the pavement: a cornerstone, a lintel, a boundary marker.

riddles.text: I still point the way to somewhere that is gone. Follow me no further than the photograph.
hints: Read the old walls.
The paint faded. The name outlived the shop.
A sign for a business or place that no longer exists.

riddles.text: Someone on this street cannot wait. Catch them celebrating the wrong season.
hints: It is October, and they have skipped ahead.
Tinsel, snowflakes, a man in a red suit.
Winter holiday decorations or sales, up before Halloween is over.

riddles.text: What have you walked past a hundred times? Tonight, bring it to me.
hints: You have been looking harder all night.
Small is fine. Ordinary is better.
Anything you noticed only because the hunt made you look.
